harness.note: The better-borg-c runner and observer at this commit build and run every specimen. A specimen is the game and Borg source at its own ref; the observer instrumentation comes from the harness commit. It applies to specimens of kind "better-borg-c" (the default). Specimens of kind "borg-rs" are built and run by borg-rs's own harness at the specimen's ref (harness/build.sh and the borgh frontend). This pin is also a specimen ref (4.2.6-bbc-9ca98661): the harness bumped with the mode-cutoff restart so runner and specimens move together (borg-zoo#54).

experiment.owner_authorization: 2026-11-24: borg-reborn-rs owner started it ("you can continue on those now", borg-reborn-rs#1175) and the zoo owner said "dispatch all" (borg-zoo#779).
experiment.prespecified: Fixed 2026-11-24, before any result (Rule 22, #758). Two builds of diegoami/borg-reborn-rs, both with the shipped harness/borg.txt: base 7c5df737 (before the fix) and fixed 3c1aa939 (the merged #1174: the exhausted fallback tries a known up staircase when the dive has no way down, and sets stair_less so caution takes it). No profile overrides - the fallback is core code, not a switch. Pilot classes-18 paired; the smoke games never reach the state (4/4 identical), so the small tier follows on a clean gate, larger tiers on the owner's word. Gate: no config_error; one binary per arm; every cell ends in death, turn_cap or borg_stopped. Progress endpoint (Rule 22): CL5 reached by 100,000 turns - known attainment out of all starts, deaths, unfinished and alive at the cutoff with CL5 reported separately; DL3/DL5 and level arrival as diagnostics. Report: paired per class against base (deaths, mean CL, max depth, rescued/newly killed, identical games); on the fixed arm the count of the fallback note "# No down stair to dive by; trying the up stairs (#1173)" (how often the new path acts) and the secret-door search count (the #1117 replay measure - the loop the fix removes); any death in either arm gets a /death-report pack with screens. Descriptive (RULES 14).
experiment.question: Does the #1173 exhausted-exit fallback (trying a known up staircase when the power dive has no way down) remove the long secret-door search loops on shallow levels, without death or progress regression?
